mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 4.0% in 80% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, increasing recession risk and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% in 70% of cases but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in 75% of cases but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 200.0), a federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 200.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline in 70% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) level below 2200.0 thousand units signals a contraction in the housing market, reducing consumer confidence and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 2200.0 in 75% of cases but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor market regimes (UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 100k), strong employment growth supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 100k, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above 2.0% in 70% of cases but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of those instances.
